topicDisplay: Christianity: Rites of Passage & Family Life

questions.q: What is the central symbol used in Christian baptism?
questions.explain: Water is poured or used for immersion in baptism to symbolise cleansing from sin and new life.

questions.q: Which words form the baptismal formula spoken during a Christian baptism?
options: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit
Blessed are the poor in spirit
This is my body, given for you
Ashes to ashes, dust to dust
questions.explain: The Trinitarian formula is spoken as water is applied, following Jesus' command in Matthew's Gospel.

questions.q: In which river was Jesus baptised by John the Baptist?
questions.explain: The Gospels record that Jesus was baptised by John the Baptist in the River Jordan.

questions.q: Which tradition typically practises believer's baptism by full immersion rather than infant baptism?
questions.explain: Baptists baptise those old enough to profess faith for themselves, using full immersion in water.

questions.q: Which traditional wedding vow phrase expresses lifelong commitment between the couple?
options: Go in peace to love and serve
questions.explain: The vow 'till death us do part' reflects the Christian belief that marriage is a lifelong union.

questions.q: Which words are traditionally spoken at the committal during a Christian funeral?
options: Ashes to ashes, dust to dust
questions.explain: 'Ashes to ashes, dust to dust' is said as the body is buried or cremated, reflecting human mortality.

questions.q: Which of the Ten Commandments most directly concerns family relationships?
options: Honour your father and your mother
questions.explain: This commandment teaches respect for parents and is central to Christian teaching on family life.

questions.q: What is a godparent's role at an infant baptism?
options: To make baptismal promises on behalf of the child and support their Christian upbringing
To pay for the baptism service
To choose the child's legal surname
To lead the congregation in Communion
questions.explain: Godparents speak the promises for the infant and pledge to help raise the child in the faith.

questions.q: Why is a white garment often used at a Christian baptism?
options: It symbolises purity and new life in Christ
It shows the person is now ordained
It marks the start of Lent
questions.explain: The white garment expresses that the baptised person is made clean and clothed with new life.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of confirmation?
options: To confirm for oneself the promises made at baptism
To be baptised for the first time
questions.explain: In confirmation a believer personally affirms the faith and receives strengthening of the Holy Spirit.

questions.q: A lit candle given at baptism is used to represent which idea?
options: The light of Christ passing to the baptised person
The end of the church service
questions.explain: The baptismal candle symbolises Christ as the light of the world now shared with the newly baptised.

questions.q: What does the exchange of rings in a Christian wedding symbolise?
options: Unending love and faithfulness between the couple
The wealth of the two families
The end of single life obligations
questions.explain: The unbroken circle of the ring represents eternal, faithful love within the marriage.

questions.q: Which belief is a Christian funeral primarily intended to express?
options: Hope in resurrection and eternal life
Fear that death is the end
questions.explain: Christian funerals proclaim the hope of resurrection and life after death through Christ.

questions.q: Why do many Christians choose to marry in a church?
options: Marriage is seen as a sacred covenant made before God
It is required by civil law
Only a church can grant a divorce
questions.explain: Christians regard marriage as a lifelong covenant blessed by God, so it is celebrated in God's house.

questions.q: What do parents and godparents promise at an infant's baptism?
options: To bring the child up in the Christian faith
To send the child to a private school
To have the child confirmed as a baby
To keep the child away from church until adulthood
questions.explain: At infant baptism the adults commit to raising the child within the Christian community and faith.

questions.q: How is the family sometimes described in Christian teaching, especially in the Catholic tradition?
options: The 'domestic church' where faith is first learned
questions.explain: The family is called the domestic church because children first learn to pray and believe at home.

questions.q: James's church baptises only adults who can declare their own faith, using full immersion in a pool. Which tradition does his church most likely belong to?
questions.explain: Believer's baptism by full immersion of those who can profess faith is characteristic of Baptist churches.

questions.q: At a Roman Catholic funeral, a service including Holy Communion is offered for the person who has died. What is this service called?
questions.explain: A Requiem Mass is the Catholic funeral Mass offered for the repose of the deceased.

questions.q: A teenager wants to take personal responsibility for the faith their godparents promised on their behalf as a baby. Which rite of passage allows this?
questions.explain: Confirmation lets a young person personally affirm the baptismal promises made for them in infancy.

questions.q: A Christian mother teaches her children to pray, reads them Bible stories and takes them to Sunday school. This best illustrates which aspect of the topic?
options: The meaning of the baptismal candle
questions.explain: Passing on prayer, scripture and worship at home is a key part of Christian religious upbringing in the family.
